correctness.rationale: An all-normal great-circle Fourier and AM--GM inequality proves the sharp convexity range and exactly twelve curvature contacts. The tangent determinant is calculated algebraically; local Hessian diag(27/4,9/8) and parameter slope sqrt6/3 are verified symbolically at every symmetry orbit. The surface area curvature change of variables uses D^(3/4), and dominated-convergence rescaling of F double prime proves its negative delta^(-1/4) singularity. Twice integrating gives the exact negative delta^(7/4) coefficient. The included standalone checker was executed, and numerical samples were not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Affine surface area is a natural curvature-sensitive valuation for the canonical nonspherical constant-width body with triple-symmetric planar projections. The exact loss of twice differentiable behavior at the maximal convex amplitude is a structural boundary phenomenon; the 12-contact coefficient and 7/4 exponent are specific, motivated, nontrivial quantities useful for evaluating deformations near degenerating curvature. The claim is not a generic textbook consequence of the already-known brightness and convexity constants alone.
